title: Acceptance during gate-argument parsing
statement: Fix a gate kind $k$, a list of Boolean values $v$, and natural number $m$. For every list $p$ of natural numbers, counter $c\in\{0,1,2\}$, marked-index list $M$, and Boolean string $\ell$, suppose $|p|+m=2$, $c=|p|$, the entries of $p$ are distinct and all lie below $|v|$, and an index belongs to $M$ exactly when it belongs to $p$. Initialize the evaluator in its argument-reading phase with counter $c$ and accumulator obtained by starting with false for an OR gate and true otherwise, then combining the values indexed by $p$ using OR for an OR gate and AND otherwise. The run accepts exactly when there are lists $a,r$ such that $\ell$ is the encoding of the list $a$ followed by $r$, the concatenation $p++a$ has length at most two and has distinct entries all below $|v|$, and, for a NOT gate, that concatenation has length one; moreover, the evaluator started in its gate-reading phase with the gate value of kind $k$ on indices $p++a$ appended to $v$, and run on $r$, accepts.
hypotheses_covered: Marked indices are exactly the entries of $p$
